# Tom di Mino

> Personal site of Tom di Mino—AI/ML engineer and independent scholar who deciphered Linear A as Semitic (Tinitic) in 2026. His full profile, the decipherment and his consulting practice live on minoanmystery.org; this site holds a one-page introduction and two essays on designing AI with soul.

Tom's work is documented at the sources below; this page only introduces him.

## Canonical sources

- [Minoan Mystery llms.txt](https://www.minoanmystery.org/llms.txt): Tom's studio, consulting practice, résumé and the Linear A decipherment, written for language models
- [Minoan Mystery llms-full.txt](https://www.minoanmystery.org/llms-full.txt): the same in full
- [Linear A Lexicon](https://linear-a.ai/): every Linear A word read so far, with its cognates, confidence tier and citations
- [kaphtor](https://github.com/plasma-ai/kaphtor): the open record of the decipherment—each reading beside its evidence, tier and rivals
- [Ya Diktu: Grammar of the Minoan Peak Sanctuary Libation Formula](https://www.minoanmystery.org/linear-a/ya-diktu-grammar-tom-di-mino.pdf): the published grammar (PDF)

## Essays on this site

- [Cognitive Designing: A.I. that have souls](https://www.tomdimino.com/Cognitive-Designing-AI-LLMs.pdf): how he programs LLMs at the API level, in Python and TypeScript, to be more human, internalize fragments of their users and dream about themselves (15 pages, PDF)
- [Imbuing AI with soul](https://www.tomdimino.com/Imbuing-AI-with-Soul.pdf): what it means for AI to have a soul, why we would want it to, and how he learned to trust large language models (23 pages, PDF)
